gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.
'Besides' means in addition to; 'beside' means next to; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: The company has changed ___ logo twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form of 'it'; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'. 'Its'' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: Her annual ___ is reviewed every April.
gaps.hint: fixed regular pay for professional work, usually monthly
gaps.explanation: 'Salary' is fixed regular pay for professional or office work, usually paid monthly; 'wages' are usually weekly.
'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: He gave a ___ summary of the 40-page report.
gaps.explanation: 'A brief summary' — adjective; 'briefly' is the adverb.

gaps.sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
gaps.hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
gaps.explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.
